$comment: The per-commit review's SECURITY CHECKLIST (operator ruling 2026-11-19, worklist #bbd0f487). Read by .claude/hooks/stop/wl_reviewsec.py, which renders the items into wl_review.PROMPT at review time under render_cap_chars, and folds the learned layer from agent/ledgers/review-security.jsonl on top. Every finding of class `security` blocks a push whatever its severity, so an item names a concrete defect a diff can show, never a general worry. Public-repo leaks are out of scope by the same ruling.
$render_cap_chars: The rendered block's ceiling in characters, base items plus the learned lines for the touched files. test-wl_review-security.py pins the shipped base well under it and the worst-case render at or under it.
$learn: wl_reviewsec.maybe_learn, run by the review child after each review at most once per every_h hours: scans the newest scan_commits commits and every record under agent/reviews/, appends proposal rows, applies them with an audit row each, and retires the oldest applied rows of a type past max_fp_notes or max_learned_items. render_fp_notes and render_learned cap the learned lines one prompt carries, and only lines about a file the commit touches are rendered.

items.text: A secret (token, key, password, private key, bws value) placed on argv, in a log line, an error message, printed output or a committed file; env or stdin carries it instead
A redaction or sensitivity check that tests only the exact key or pointer it is handed and misses nested fields, arrays or a parent object
examples: `rdc config field get --pointer /credentials` printed every secret below the parent pointer

items.text:
A secret read outside the bws_env profiles (`bws_env exec --profile

`): a hard-coded value, a new .env file, or a token copied into a config or a workflow env block
A shell command string built from input (repo name, path, config or user value) without quoting: renet runs it as root and the CLI sends it over ssh; an argv array or shell quoting is safe
A D1 or other SQL query built by concatenation or template interpolation instead of bound parameters (`.bind()`)
A path from input used by sync, sftp, a file write or an extract without refusing `..`, an absolute path or a symlink that escapes the target directory
An account Worker route whose auth, tenant (org or team) or role check is removed, weakened, moved after the data access, or skipped on an error path
A GitHub workflow that widens `permissions:`, checks out the PR head under `pull_request_target` or `workflow_run`, or interpolates `${{ github.event.* }}` into a `run:` script
A hook, guard or gate changed so it can no longer refuse: a fail-open on error, an environment bypass, a widened allowlist, or a test that no longer reaches the refusal
